detail:
Live one-shot for OpenCode qualification candidate eeeab7e6 (agentops#2142)
failed pre-provider on 2026-08-12T06:34:39Z: worker boundary probe failed
because gitops-nixos modules/system/opencode-qualification.nix set
stateRoot (/var/lib/agentops/opencode-qualification) tmpfiles mode to
0700 root:root, blocking agentworker's traversal into workspaces/<run-id>
beneath it even though workspaces/ itself was 0711. No provider contact,
no spend. Fixed to 0711 in gitops-nixos commit 3b5b062, redeployed to
devbox, traversal and --verify-installation reconfirmed clean.

The failed attempt wrote permanent-by-design ledger files for packet
sha256:e5deca96d596d537a2b6459a987199153ca88d18d2c2a9620fd55d3fcad94226:
ledger/packet.attempted and
ledger/nonce-6b2b0ab6045fe978bf283381f5a8d3ff96b891861147b6593d88f860d83380d6.issued.
Operator (bayleaf) reviewed the failure as infra-only (not a packet/corpus
defect) and authorized clearing the sentinel for a fresh attempt on this
same packet rather than waiting for a re-issued corpus. Per that
authorization: both files archived read-only (0400) to
/var/lib/agentops/opencode-qualification/evidence/archived-attempts/2026-08-12T06-34-39Z/
on devbox before removal from ledger/, then removed from ledger/ to permit
a fresh --verify-installation-clean live attempt on this identical packet.
summary: Archived and cleared burned one-shot sentinel for eeeab7e6 qualification packet after fixing infra bug; authorized fresh rerun

detail:
Operator (bayleaf) authorized clearing the previous infra-caused sentinel
and rerunning; explicitly authorized real provider spend for this retry
(see ad:01KZTGBZCC8AAVBMHA8F6XGDYW).

Second attempt (run-c6efc65844a1503d9a4a096c6e47ac77, session
ses_00af917fdffeGam5qTU0bU4LLi, packet sha256:e5deca96...) actually
invoked OpenCode against opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash and failed
runner-side receipt validation: "one-shot run did not produce exactly
one provider-origin step-finish". opencode.log shows two separate
provider streams: one for OpenCode's automatic session-title generation
(agent=title, small=true) and one for the actual task
(agent=ao-mechanical-bulk, small=false). Both are real provider calls;
real spend occurred on both.

Root cause is in the pinned corpus content itself, not gitops-nixos or
devbox: /etc/agentops/opencode-qualification/opencode.hybrid.json (byte-
identical to the previously reviewed 0d267773 revision) has no setting
disabling OpenCode's automatic title generation, so every fresh session
deterministically produces a second provider-origin step-finish before
the runner ever gets a clean one-event receipt.

This is not a transient/infra failure -- a bare retry on this identical
packet/config will reproduce the same rejection and spend again with
certainty. No further rerun attempted. Recommend: fix upstream in
agentops (disable auto-title in opencode.hybrid.json, or accept
provider-origin step-finish counting logic disambiguates the title
call), cut a new reviewed revision, and treat this packet as failed
pending that fix -- not pending another local-only retry.
summary: Fresh eeeab7e6 one-shot rejected post-provider: two step-finish events (auto-title + main), spend occurred; do not blind-retry

detail:
Per note #2372 (devbox review, commit 79174c0: "fix: pass explicit
session title and add bounded diagnostics on step-finish mismatch"),
this directly fixes the root cause of the second failed live attempt
(ad:01KZTGJ6499E4V2FMY8KNTMYWS) -- OpenCode's automatic session-title

against gitops-nixos main, branch
agent/opencode-qualification-2142-v2, commit 482380a), refreshed the

locally, deployed to devbox, --verify-installation clean.

packet_digest is unchanged (sha256:e5deca96...) from the failed
eeeab7e6 attempt -- expected: the corpus diff only updates its
runner_digest cross-reference field to match the fixed runner; the
actual packet content (task/oracle/gates) is untouched, so this is a
bugfix to the same logical packet, not a new one.

Archived the spend-incurring second attempt's sentinel
(ledger/packet.attempted) and consumed nonce to
evidence/archived-attempts/2026-08-12T08-11-11Z/ before clearing them
from ledger/, under the operator's standing spend authorization
(carried in note #2372) so a fresh attempt with the fix in place can

summary: Cleared spend-incurring attempt sentinel to run agentops#2142 note #2372 fix (79174c0, auto-title mismatch remediated)

detail:
Deployed gitops-nixos candidate bump to 79174c0 (branch
agent/opencode-qualification-2142-v2, commit 482380a; PR not yet
opened), fixing the auto-title double-call bug per note #2372. Cleared
the prior spend-incurring sentinel (ad:01KZV6RBTE82MR8KEKFMRF7AZ6) and
fired a fresh attempt (run-4e9c5460d5d00afbf87e24ea25f4b35f, session
ses_00992e890ffe24TITnNxBu56sQ).

Confirmed the fix worked as intended: opencode.log shows exactly one
provider stream this time (agent=ao-mechanical-bulk only, explicit
session title "agentops-qualification-run-..." set, no separate
agent=title call).

But the runner still rejected the run: "one-shot run did not produce
exactly one provider-origin step-finish (observed 0 provider events, 0
recorded): []". execute_once()'s subprocess exited 0 (not the "run
failed with exit N" path) and the stream genuinely started per the
log, so this is very likely a new, distinct bug -- the event-parsing
loop in run_opencode_qualification.py (added/changed alongside the
auto-title fix per the same 79174c0 commit) is not recognizing the
step-finish event OpenCode actually emitted, not a case of the run
never contacting the provider. Spend likely occurred a third time.

Did not retry further. Archived this attempt's sentinel and nonce to
evidence/archived-attempts/2026-08-12T14-42-51Z/ and left ledger/
burned (packet.attempted NOT cleared this time) pending human review
of the new event-parsing bug -- this is now two distinct live-only
bugs found in two different corpus revisions of the same packet, both
only surfaced by actually spending money, so a third blind retry is
not warranted without upstream investigation of _provider_event()/
_provider_usage() against whatever step-finish shape OpenCode 1.18.4
+ opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash actually emits for this exact
config/agent (ao-mechanical-bulk, explicit title, no small=true call).
summary: Third eeeab7e6/79174c0 attempt: auto-title bug fixed (confirmed single stream call), but run produced 0 provider-origin step-finish events; likely new bug, spend likely occurred, stopped without retry

detail:
Operator (bayleaf) reviewed the design pass recorded at
ad:01KZV9KAYH82ZBKVG2X9N7SNJE / sprintctl event #2375 and authorized
devbox to implement it as designed: no further scope negotiation
requested, no alternate option chosen. Implementation should cover the
full scope identified in the design, not just execute_once():

- run_opencode_qualification.py: _provider_event() gates on
  step_finish + valid sessionID + successful _provider_usage() bound
  checks; drop provider_request_id as a hard requirement; keep
  extracting it as optional/non-authoritative when present.
- validate_opencode_qualification.py: the mandatory-key checks on
  provider_request_id_digest (runner_record.usage, receipt.usage_evidence,
  and the two provider_request_id_digest == source_event_digest
  cross-checks) become conditional on the field's presence, or the
  schema is redefined so absence is the expected/valid case.
- docs/dispatch/opencode-provider-qualification-corpus.md: rewrite the
  "Provider origin is carried by..." paragraph to describe the actual
  mechanism (usage/cost bound-checks + independent sanitized-export
  cross-check, no provider-issued opaque ID claimed), plus a
  remediation section documenting this root-cause history.
- test_run_opencode_qualification.py: _event() fixture and any test
  asserting request-ID-gating behavior need a no-request-ID case
  (matching the real captured shape) as the regression test that
  should have existed originally.
- Receipt/record schema version bump (v2 -> v3) since the evidentiary
  meaning of usage_evidence/provider_model_evidence changes.

Standing note carried forward: this fix does not resurrect either
burned packet (eeeab7e6, 79174c0 attempts); a new packet_digest is
required for any future live attempt regardless of this change.
summary: Operator authorized devbox to implement the provider-origin-proof redesign as specified in the design pass (ad:01KZV9KAYH82ZBKVG2X9N7SNJE)

detail:
Follow-up design pass after the operator reframed #2142 from
"provider-qualified" attestation down to a weak admission smoke test
("can we route to it, is output reasonable for cost") and explicitly
deprioritized the stronger continuous-fitness system to agentops#2143.
Read the full branch tip (634ffd4) end to end, not just the doc.

Delete outright:
- Ed25519 signing key / allowed_signers / signed runner record --
  verified no downstream logic depends on signed-ness distinct from the
  plaintext fields it re-derives; qualification_eligible was hardcoded
  False regardless of signature validity.
- Permanent O_EXCL ledger sentinel (ledger/packet.attempted) -- directly
  contradicts "repeatable sanity check, not one-shot commitment";
  replaced by nothing more than an optional cooldown against accidental
  loop-spend, easily overridden.
- Both independent-human-review gates (before and after) -- nothing is
  promoted or committed by this check, so nothing needs commitment-grade
  review. verify_and_consume_opencode_qualification.py deleted outright.
- ~400 lines of pinned-executable/resolved-parent-chain/Nix-store-mount
  fingerprinting machinery and the root-owned digest-pinned install tree
  for the corpus/profile/policy/manifest/runner itself -- attestation-
  grade supply-chain ceremony, not something that affects routability or
  cost-sanity. Separated from credential protection, which is kept.
- Optional/non-gating request-ID plumbing from the prior redesign --
  dead weight now that it's confirmed to never appear in real output;
  trivial to re-add if ever observed.

Keep and shrink:
- _provider_usage() bound-checks (positive baseline, finite cost, ratio
  ceiling) -- this is the real "reasonable for cost" answer, kept as-is.
- _parse_sanitized_export() independent providerID/modelID/finish
  cross-check -- the real "routable" answer, kept but with the exact
  part-grammar match loosened (over-fitted to one harness snapshot).
- "Exactly one step-finish event, hard-fail on any other count" loosened
  to "at least one clean completion event, sanity-bound all of them" --
  the exact-count strictness is itself flagged as over-fit security-gate
  behavior inappropriate for a sanity check, and is what already caused
  the false "auto-title" diagnosis earlier in this thread.
- Containment/worker-boundary probe kept essentially as-is -- cheap,
  mechanical, answers a real and distinct "not obviously dangerous"
  question. Only trimmed to stop routing through the deleted pinned-
  executable-chain machinery.
- Credential provisioning/scrub discipline (0400, disposable per-run
  copy, wipe-and-scan-after) kept unchanged -- explicitly separated as
  the one thing that still needs real protection.

Generalization: identified which pieces are OpenCode-specific (export
format, event-stream shape, pinned executable set, version check) vs.
already harness-agnostic (usage bound-check shape, containment-probe
pattern, credential-scrub pattern, the overall two-question shape).
Explicitly declined to build a harness abstraction layer now -- only
one implementation exists; factor common shape out when a second
harness actually appears, not speculatively.

Before/after workflow specified: operator runs one script directly
(no packet freeze, no sudoers boundary beyond credential access, no
review gate), gets one JSON result (routability + cost-sanity +
containment + pass/fail), a plain run-report log entry, reruns
immediately on failure with no ledger to reset.

Design only, no code written. Files scoped: run_opencode_qualification.py
(mostly deleted, remainder becomes the new checker),
validate_opencode_qualification.py (signature/ledger logic deleted,
receipt-shape validation shrunk), verify_and_consume_opencode_qualification.py
(deleted outright), the corpus JSON (shrunk), the doc (rewritten).
summary: Second design pass: right-sized admission check for OpenCode -- deletes signing chain, permanent ledger, dual review gates; shrinks pinning to credential-only; keeps usage/cost bound-check, sanitized-export cross-check, containment probe

detail:
Root cause from ad:01KZVDY1ZV960SSTNBH4HJ8FG2 was a headless tool-permission
fallthrough triggered by the admission check's own default prompt, not a
model problem and not a production dispatch config problem -- deliberately
scoped the fix to check_opencode_admission.py's --prompt default only,
left templates/dispatch/hybrid/opencode.hybrid.json (shared with
production hybrid-dispatch) untouched. Pushed to
origin/codex/agentops-2142 (6dfb3df).

Reran on devbox (/home/dev/agentops-admission-check, fast-forwarded to
6dfb3df): pass=true. routable=true, cost_sane=true, cost_usd=0.000313908,
usage_multiplier=1.007, containment=pass, export_cross_check
finish=stop/providerID=opencode-go/modelID=deepseek-v4-flash,
completion_events=1. Run report written to
docs/dispatch/admission-runs/opencode-opencode-go-deepseek-v4-flash-2026-08-12.json
in the devbox checkout -- no signature, no root-owned install, no
ledger entry, exactly the plain non-privileged record the redesign
specified.

This is the first successful end-to-end exercise of the redesigned
admission check after: root-cause correction (auto-title retraction),
two design passes (narrow provider-origin-proof fix, then the full
attestation-to-admission-check redesign), implementation + independent
review on devbox (96706e4, 74d3d04), gitops-nixos module rewrite
(gitops-nixos#14), and this prompt fix. Total live spend across the
whole investigation: two failed attempts under the old design
(real spend, exact amounts not captured) plus this session's
$0.000333158 (failed) + $0.000313908 (passed) under the new design --
the "cheap" premise held up in practice.

Open, not addressed here: whether real production hybrid-dispatch runs
hit the same "*": "ask" headless fallthrough for bash/edit/write via
opencode.hybrid.json. Flagged, not investigated.
summary: Fixed the default admission-check prompt (6dfb3df); rerun passed cleanly -- opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash routable, cost-sane, contained

detail:
Per operator direction ("nothing is running, safe to touch the broad
file now, this will be run much more later"): investigated whether
templates/dispatch/hybrid/opencode.hybrid.json's base permission
("*": "ask") could be changed without affecting production hybrid
dispatch. Confirmed from hybrid_dispatch.py's build_overlay(): every
real dispatch invocation builds and passes a fully-resolved,
packet-specific permission block that completely replaces the base
config's permission map -- the base file's wildcard is never read by
production. The only current consumer of the raw base permission is
the admission check itself.

Resolved the base permission explicitly (651c14e), mirroring
build_overlay's own already-validated pattern (its docstring documents
why a blanket "*": "deny" is wrong -- withholds tools from the model
entirely): read/glob/grep/list/todowrite/todoread/edit/write/patch ->
allow (containment already comes from the disposable per-run workspace
+ external_directory: deny, same reasoning production uses), bash ->
fully closed ({"*": "deny"}), matching production's own fallback-closed
default before any packet-specific command allowlist is added.

validate_hybrid_dispatch.py hard-asserted base["*"] == "ask" as a named
security invariant ("the checked-in base config must not pre-authorize
anything") -- would have KeyError'd on the new shape. Did not delete
the check; rewrote it to assert the actual invariant this config
family cares about: no wildcard fallback left unresolved, and bash
specifically denied by default (no containment equivalent exists for
unscoped bash execution the way there is for edit/write). Ran the full
existing test suite against the real files: 65/65 pass in
test_hybrid_dispatch.py including test_rejects_a_worker_config_that_pre_authorizes_bash;
62/63 in the check/probe/validator suites combined, with the one
failure a pre-existing environment path gap on this host
(/run/current-system/sw/bin doesn't exist off-NixOS), unrelated to
this change.

Pulled to devbox's /home/dev/agentops-admission-check checkout and
reran the live admission check against the new config: pass=true,
cost_usd=0.000220108, routable, contained, finish=stop -- confirms the
broader fix didn't change observed model behavior for this check.

Pushed to origin/codex/agentops-2142 (651c14e), on top of the earlier
narrow prompt fix (6dfb3df).
summary: Fixed opencode.hybrid.json's headless ask-fallback (651c14e), confirmed zero production impact, updated the validator invariant to match, reran clean

detail:
PR #36 (codex/agentops-2142 -> main) had 8 real conflicts against main,
not incidental noise: docs/plans/harness-profile-qualification.md,
docs/runbooks/hybrid-dispatch.md, harness-profile.schema.json,
opencode-nixpkgs-devbox-1.18.4.json, probe_opencode_profile.py (add/add),
validate_harness_profiles.py, test_probe_opencode_profile.py (add/add),
test_validate_harness_profiles.py -- caused by main independently
merging e031db4 ("feat(dispatch): harden opencode lifecycle profile")
after this branch was cut.

Investigated rather than blind-resolved: diffed f50a8d2 (same commit
message, on the branch) against e031db4 (on main) directly -- byte
identical patch content, just reached via different commit paths
(cherry-pick or parallel authorship of the same work). Confirmed
main's current content for all 8 files exactly matches the branch's
state at that shared point, and main never touched them again --
meaning the branch's version (which continued with 3 more commits:
6dc2479, 47e6de6, 0d26777, building the qualification/admission-check
work on top) is a strict superset, not a real divergence.

Resolved by taking the branch's version for all 8 files (git checkout
--ours after a normal merge, not a blanket -X ours which would have
risked discarding main's other unrelated changes -- e.g. the cockpit
completion-alerts work that also landed on main in the interim).
Verified all 8 resolved files byte-match origin/codex/agentops-2142's
content before committing. Ran the merged tree's test suite:
136/137 pass (the 1 failure is the same pre-existing off-NixOS
environment gap noted in ad:01KZVF0ZZP9KDSKQVJ0137RN0F, unrelated).

Merged via gh (regular merge commit, matching repo convention, not
squash) as c1e8b042cbd383a307ee90a913bd529cd6fecf1d. Updated devbox's
/home/dev/agentops-admission-check checkout to track main and reran
the live admission check post-merge: still pass=true, $0.000216678.

agentops#2142's full arc is now on main: root-cause correction,
redesign, both live-fire fixes, and this merge.
summary: agentops#36 merged to main (c1e8b04): admission-check redesign is now on agentops main, confirmed still passing
